negative_results: Worthlessness/guilt wording was not stable: pooled prevalence was 45.5% diagnosed versus 43.6% control, but fold 2 reversed and fold 3 was nearly tied.
Bereavement/loss language showed essentially no separation: 13.6% versus 12.6% overall, with controls higher in fold 2.
Politics/news language did not distinguish groups: 61.3% diagnosed versus 62.1% control overall, with mixed fold directions.
Basic sleep, appetite, loneliness, and sadness terms were common in both groups; they should not be treated as specific evidence without self-reference, persistence, or co-occurring domains.
URLs, hashtags, and emoji were almost absent, suggesting preprocessing or collection artifacts rather than useful behavioral signals.
